body:
INDEPENDENT IMPLEMENTATION / RENDERER REVIEW — codex-mockup-implementation-review (read-only).

Artifact inspected: storyatlas4s/mockups/mockup1.png, 1536 x 1024, SHA-256 d136675d7b11e6c1197026483662812f16766bbb71051ffcf9611ad00fb3d6ce. It is untracked at storyatlas4s c9f9e365dd6668af95f19b7ac4d4e33c40343a53. Renderer comparison is against Intaglio 596b398af380079e4b251535230d0bc03cd88c51.

VERDICT

The composition is implementable as a hybrid application and is useful for defining coordination among surfaces. It is not implementable faithfully as one giant Intaglio scene, nor should it be. Intaglio is sufficient for the first real, SVG-based WOG slice. The mockup nevertheless implies unproven capabilities—dense interactive rendering, collision-aware graph labels, generic picking/culling, stable animated relayout, and whole-workspace export—that need typed spikes and measurements. Nothing here justifies a new general visualization layer or an off-the-shelf graph package yet.

OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY

1. Laminar/DOM should own the CSS-grid shell, tabs, presets, tree, controls, inspector, page chrome, keyboard focus, search, copy/selection, and all canonical prose. The Codex text must remain actual DOM text; it cannot become glyphs in SVG/Canvas. Responsive layout should dock or hide secondary surfaces rather than uniformly shrink this 1536 x 1024 composition—the prose is already near the legibility floor in the mockup.

2. storymodel4s view artifacts should own semantic truth and placement. This is not a new screen-level scene graph. Compile separate CodexFlow / paginated Codex and NarrativeScene plates under one CommonViewState; when recall views exist, compile their typed artifact separately and join through the match-checked trace. The app composes plates. The inspector reads audit/provenance structures, never labels scraped back from rendered geometry.

3. Intaglio SVG should initially own Atlas regions, landmarks, paths, labels, Codex brackets/bands/arcs/portals, selection outlines, and small overview/track graphics. Current Intaglio already has immutable scenes, groups, rectangles/polygons, points, lines, text, viewports/clipping, deterministic JVM/JS SVG, and caller-supplied data-name markers.

4. Canvas should be an underlay only after a benchmark demonstrates SVG failure (for dense tracks, terrain, or population recall). Current Canvas can draw an Intaglio scene but has no name-keyed bounds or hit-test API; names are discarded during drawing. Making the interactive map Canvas-first would therefore discard the working browser/SVG picking path and create an immediate accessibility burden.

IDENTITY, PICKING, AND SELECTION

5. GraphicsName is a renderer marker, not story identity, and Intaglio permits duplicate names. The adapter must continue the current injective rules: Atlas groups named by MarkId; flow overlays by AnnotationId; paginated overlays by FragmentId. These are three separate identity domains and must never be union-compared. A NavigationIndex resolves each interactive marker exactly once to a typed address; shared semantic selection remains Set[Address], many rendered marks to one address.

6. SVG picking is viable now: delegated DOM events can climb to the nearest data-name group, and the existing SvgDom helper already supplies keyboard reachability, roles, labels, aria-pressed, and selected classes. Clicking the node circle, its text, or its group must resolve identically. The inspector must not open for a merely decorative unnamed child.

7. The mockup makes every mark look individually pickable even when paths cross or labels overlap. That is not yet guaranteed. Any bundling, label hiding, stacking, or aggregation must retain every member MarkId and a descent path. Occlusion is a correctness issue: a rendered mark that cannot be pointed to or reached by keyboard has failed the identity law even if its data-name remains in the XML.

CAMERA, LAYOUT, LABELS, AND LOD

8. The Atlas graph itself is drawable in Intaglio SVG, but Intaglio does not lay it out. Coordinates, z-order, visible semantic marks, relation filtering, and label priority must be deterministic compiler/layout results upstream. The “Layout: Chronological” control must compile a typed projection/ViewSpec with a visible ProjectionContract; it must not invoke an ad-hoc browser graph layout. Pan/zoom can initially be app-owned camera state lowered to one root Viewport. Intaglio supports the necessary scale/translation/clipping, but has no general camera object or screen-to-world inverse.

9. There is no generic label collision or priority engine. The mockup’s node labels therefore require a deterministic label-candidate pass using receipted text metrics, stable priorities, bounded visible labels, and an accessible route to every hidden label. “Show Labels” is visibly unchecked while labels are displayed; define this as “secondary labels” or fix the state. Label visibility is scientific view state and belongs in the saved specification.

10. Intaglio has no semantic LOD or viewport culling, correctly: storymodel4s must choose visible parents/children under the evidence horizon and preserve OnMark / ViaAncestor / OffProjection. The app must range-query a bounded visible set before lowering. Intaglio currently resolves the complete supplied scene.

11. Intaglio scenes are immutable and there is no incremental scene diff or morph system. Replacing the whole SVG is acceptable for WOG. Stable animated projection switches or parent-to-child morphs need explicit correspondence supplied by the view artifact, app-owned interpolation, a reduced-motion path, and measurement; similarity of labels or coordinates is not correspondence.

12. The top “Codex” tab appears active while Atlas and Recall are simultaneously prominent, and “View Presets” duplicates the bottom “View Modes.” Implementation needs one serializable canonical view state: a docked Codex plus one primary projection, optional secondary plate, declared relation/feature layers, and responsive panel state. Two unrelated control systems will otherwise produce irreproducible combinations.

FEATURE AND RECALL SURFACES

13. The overview and sensory plots are feasible as small SVG scenes. If they become token-dense, Canvas is a candidate after measurement. A scalar feature plate must carry value, coverage, validity/missingness, reducer/window, normalization, and provider receipt separately. Current Intaglio ScalarField2D accepts total finite fields but has no coverage-aware mask through contouring. For the first slice, render supported rectangles plus an explicit missingness mask; never encode missing as zero or transparent “low.”

14. Detailed recall links are feasible as named SVG polylines or tessellated ribbons. Intaglio has no cubic path primitive, so smooth ribbons are adapter-side deterministic tessellation until that demonstrably fails. Every state—including Unranked/abstention, External, distortion facets, multimodality, and posterior mass—must remain selectable and non-colour-only. A population matrix/overview should not be promoted to Canvas until SVG mark/pick measurements fail.

EXPORT, SHARING, AND RECEIPTS

15. “Export View” currently conflates three products: (a) deterministic export of one graphics plate, which Intaglio SVG/Java2D can support; (b) a hybrid workspace/page figure containing DOM text plus overlays, which needs the existing static-HTML/print or browser capture pipeline; and (c) a saved interactive state, which is serialized data, not an image. Give these separate commands.

16. Every saved/shareable view must bind at least model/source checksums, CommonViewState/ViewSpec, projection contract, horizon, focus/selection, camera and dock state, active relation layers, feature sidecar/normalization/window/coverage receipt, pagination/text-metrics/font receipt, renderer/backend and software versions, and any recall trace/checksum. A PNG alone is not reproducible evidence. Exported graphics and the deterministic textual twin must descend from the same portable artifact.

CONCRETE SPIKES AND BENCHMARK GATES

A. Identity/picking spike: mount one exact-source WOG Codex page plus Story/Episode/Scene Atlas plates; enumerate MarkId, AnnotationId, and FragmentId sets separately; prove marker injection/navigation totality; click and keyboard-activate shape and label children; prove one Address selection survives as OnMark, ViaAncestor with descent path, or OffProjection across zoom/horizon changes.

B. Camera/occlusion/labels spike: generated named regions, landmarks, long crossing routes, and labels under nested clipping and root-Viewport pan/zoom. Measure delegated-pick latency; prove z-order; deliberately overlap marks and labels; require every aggregated/hidden member to remain discoverable and reachable. Compare deterministic label choices under the saved metrics receipt.

C. Performance ladder: use actual WOG plus generated region, landmark, path, text, and mixed workloads across increasing visible mark counts, and separately a large total artifact that returns the same bounded visible sets. Record portable compile, Intaglio lowering/allocation, DeviceScene resolution, SVG serialization bytes/time, DOM injection, pick latency, full camera frame time, and Canvas draw time. Use repeated runs in the installed project browser. Retain the agreed gates: ordinary pan/zoom at 60 fps, cached semantic LOD under 100 ms, and a declared viewport mark budget. Promote Canvas/WebGL/tiles/workers only after a named workload misses a gate and the candidate fixes it.

D. Feature-mask spike: same numerical feature with supported, low-coverage, and missing cells; prove missing never becomes zero and contours/selection do not cross unsupported regions. This is the evidence needed before proposing a generic coverage-aware Intaglio scalar field.

E. Recall-path spike: an alignment matrix and detailed trace containing Exact, Distorted, External, Unranked, branching posterior mass, and a misordered crossing. Compare straight/tessellated SVG paths for size, draw time, pickability, and preservation of every state; only then consider a native curve primitive.

F. Export spike: from one saved receipt, regenerate the individual SVG plate, hybrid static Codex/Atlas page, textual twin, and saved state; verify stable identities and hashes where the layout inputs are identical, and make differing browser text metrics explicit rather than silently claiming byte identity.

DISPOSITION

Keep this PNG as a speculative composition reference only. A faithful next artifact should be generated from real typed view artifacts, exact DOM text, and the existing Intaglio SVG lowering. The first implementation risk is not drawing circles or charts; it is preserving identity, evidence, selection, label/pick visibility, and receipts across the many coordinated surfaces shown here.
